articles.title: ‘Paper Tiger’ Producer Rodrigo Teixeira Set for GLAFF’s First Visionary Award, Presented by Wagner Moura (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: Two-time Oscar-nominated producer Rodrigo Teixeira will receive the inaugural Árbol de la Vida Visionary Award at the GuadaLAjara Film Festival (GLAFF), the Los Angeles offshoot of the Guadalajara International Film Festival, on Nov. 6.
body: “Rodrigo Teixeira has built a career defined by bold storytelling and a true commitment to artists across the border,” says Ximena Urrutia, executive director of GLAFF. “As inaugural mentor of our New Mexico-U. S. co-production lab, he will help emerging filmmakers turn ambitious cross-border projects into lasting partnerships.”

For more than two decades, Teixeira has bridged Latin American and global filmmaking through his production company RT Features, whose credits include “Call Me by Your Name,” “The Lighthouse,” “The Witch” and “Invisible Life.” He earned best picture nominations for “Call Me by Your Name” and Walter Salles’ “I’m Still Here,” which won the Oscar for international feature. Films from his banner have collected nine Oscar nominations and six Golden Globe nominations.

The 16th edition of GLAFF runs Nov. 5-7 in Los Angeles, opening with Diego Luna’s “Ashes” and closing with Eddie Sánchez’s “Mexicanamerican.”

articles.title: ‘Glee’ Reboot: Who’s Coming Back? Will Rachel Sing Olivia Rodrigo? How MAGA Is Sue? And More Fan Questions
articles.summary: What have we missed on “Glee”? For six glorious, terrifying seasons from 2009 to 2015, we witnessed Ryan Murphy bring a fever dream to life. With each new episode, the musical dramedy series’ unique blend of satire and earnestness had girls, the gays and their allies pondering: What song that…
body: McKinley High School cheer coach Sue Sylvester (played by the inimitable Jane Lynch) once called herself “horny with fear,” and while we won’t go that far… we understand what she meant. So Variety ‘s resident gleeks got together and listened to the only version of “Teenage Dream” we recognize to inspire this list of our burning questions about the new “Glee.”

Depending on which characters end up returning, there are two semi-obvious (and somewhat non-forced) routes the “Glee” reboot can take. The show ended 11 years ago, so it would totally make sense to center new episodes around William McKinley High School throwing a 10-year reunion that brings back a ton of the original cast. High school culture has changed dramatically in the last decade, so perhaps the reboot finds the original glee club feeling like fish out of water as they contend with rapidly different teenage norms as they meet the school’s current glee club and show them the ropes.

articles.title: Alexander Skarsgård on His Wacky ‘Wicker’ Red Carpet Looks: From Clear Shoes and a Multicolored Skirt to a Gray Wig Inspired by Co-Star Olivia Colman
articles.summary: Alexander Skarsgård knows how to make an entrance. The Swedish actor has been turning heads with his wacky red carpet looks while promoting his new fantasy romance “Wicker.” At the London premiere earlier this month, he donned a metallic gold Saint Laurent suit.
body: At the “Wicker” premiere in Los Angeles on Tuesday, Skarsgård wore a multicolored skirt and a whimsical black shirt adorned with his co-star Olivia Colman’s face from London fashion house Chopova Lowena. “We’ve been on a press tour for a couple of weeks, and now we’re in L.A., and it’s our final big premiere before the movie opens on Friday,” he said. “I wanted to wear something special for this lovely lady over here, Olivia, whom I adore.”
As for the purple and green skirt, Skarsgård said, “It’s very comfortable. It’s quite a hot night, and it’s light and breezy. I’m enjoying it.”

Earlier in the day, he shocked attendees at a SAG-AFTRA screening and Q&A when he arrived in a long gray wig. “I got a little jealous because everyone is complimenting Olivia on her beautiful hair and beautiful hair color,” Skarsgård said. “I got no love for my hair. As a narcissistic actor, I need a little bit of attention, so I threw on a beautiful gray wig to match Olivia today.”
“Wicker” co-star Elizabeth Debicki praised Skarsgård’s fashion choices. “He can do no wrong,” she said. “I love the man. What can I say? I’m biased.”

articles.title: ‘A vehicle to expose prejudice, bias, and stupidity’: Sacha Baron Cohen defends Ali G as satire
articles.summary: The actor defended his new film, Ali G: Who Iz I?, saying his aim is to bring people ‘face-to-face with the danger of fanaticism and conspiracy theories’ Sacha Baron Cohen has launched an impassioned defence of satire, the right to offend, and his Ali G character on in a lengthy article for Time…
body: On the eve of the release of his new film, Ali G: Who Iz I?, Baron Cohen described satire as “more important than ever”, adding that “along the way, some people, instead of laughing, wince or worse, take offence.”

Comparing modern satirists to the traditional figure of the “bouffon”, Baron Cohen described satire as “the humour of the dispossessed … using biting and at times cruel humour to undermine systemic injustice”.

Having previously released films containing controversial characters including Kazakh journalist Borat Sagdiyev, Austrian fashion show presenter Brüno Gehard, and a thinly disguised Colonel Gaddafi parody called Admiral General Aladeen, Baron Cohen directly took on critics of the Ali G character, who has been criticised in the past for laughing at black street culture and described as a “black caricature”.

Baron Cohen writes: “I made this latest film for the same reason I’ve always done this work. Not only to make people laugh, but also to bring them face-to-face with the danger of fanaticism and conspiracy theories.”

articles.title: ‘I’m always being real’: what on earth persuades disgraced people like Elizabeth Holmes to let the cameras in?
articles.summary: With You Can See Everything, Holmes joins other such high-profile subjects as Lance Armstrong, Imelda Marcos and Anthony Weiner to allow film-makers to document their lives. But do they ever come out well?
body: That question of authenticity is at the heart of documentary film-making. You Can See Everything is as much about the ambiguous relationship between film-maker and subject as it is about Holmes herself. There is often a power struggle over narrative control in documentaries, with both sides of the dynamic wanting different outcomes from the final film. Watching You Can See Everything inevitably prompts the question: why would Holmes, days before she heads to jail, invite the scrutiny of a film crew?

Some people, like Holmes, think a documentary will help rebuild their reputation after public disgrace. When Anthony Weiner, who resigned from Congress after tweeting a photo of his bulging groin, tried to stage a professional comeback with a New York mayoral bid, he allowed cameras to film the journey. Only, he had more to hide: when further sex scandals emerged, his campaign went from a story of public redemption to innuendo-laden humiliation. And all the while, the cameras kept rolling. Weiner is a prime example of a subject losing control of the narrative.

articles.title: Radio presenter's 'wobbles' over Children in Need cycling challenge
articles.summary: Owain Wyn Evans says the 400-mile challenge doesn't "feel like a thing I'm able to do".
body: Radio presenter Owain Wyn Evans has voiced fears about his upcoming challenge to cycle through all four UK nations for Children in Need.
The host of BBC Radio 2's Early Breakfast Show admitted he has had "wobbles", adding: "I just don't feel like it's a thing I'm able to do."
It will see him travel almost 400 miles (643km), setting off from Glasgow and finishing in Cardiff, and is the greatest distance anyone has covered in a Radio 2 fundraising challenge.
With just 19 days to go before he is due to set off, he told colleague Sara Cox on the BBC Radio 2 Breakfast Show on Wednesday he was "so not ready".

articles.title: Clayface review – flesh-stretching DC body horror is very gory but not very good
articles.summary: Liverpool makes for an unconvincing Gotham City in this effectively gross but otherwise middling attempt to milk money from a lesser-known Batman villain. A sense of desperation is understandably in the air over at DC, the company, like Marvel, slowly realising that the mass superhero fever has…
body: Clayface is overwhelmingly not a moment. Admittedly its targets are way lower (Mike Flanagan’s original script, allegedly more texturally complex, was entirely rewritten ) but even as a similarly new way in, as a relatively standalone horror movie for those who wouldn’t now rush toward a superhero caper, it’s a clumsily missed opportunity and another reminder that those at DC don’t seem to know what they’re doing and why they’re doing it.

Gotham is where working-class boy done good Matt (Welsh actor Tom Rhys Harries, fine enough) is from and a place that he was desperate to leave. He’s a rising movie star, riding high after his first Oscar nomination (“Nominees don’t wait in line!”) and on a trip back to his home town, he makes the mistake of sleeping with the girlfriend of a violent gangster, introduced by Goldfrapp’s Ooh La La, one of the film’s many dated attempts at cool. As a result, he has his money-making face sliced up by goons and his career soon crumbles, back to a bedsit with all his money wasted on useless surgeries orchestrated by his viperous lawyer.

articles.title: UK cinemas report ‘bonkers’ demand for documentary You Can See Everything
articles.summary: Tickets for film about Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes said to be selling out after $15m opening weekend in the US. It is the film everyone seems to be talking about, spawning memes and fuelling feverish online debate about its subject, the disgraced Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes.
body: Now, a month before Nathan Fielder’s documentary You Can See Everything reaches UK cinemas, tickets for screenings are already selling out after its remarkable $15m (£11.3m) opening weekend in the US.
Clare Binns, the creative director of Picturehouse Cinemas, said the excitement was reminiscent of the response to Greta Gerwig’s Barbie, which became a global box-office phenomenon in 2023.
“People are hungry in a way that we haven’t really seen since then,” she said. “And for it to be a three-hour documentary, it’s bonkers.”

Tickets for the film, which opens in the UK on 20 November, went on sale at Picturehouse Central in London before its US opening, Binns said, and demand has prompted the chain to add extra screenings. At the Ritzy in Brixton, the first screen had almost sold out, leading the cinema to sell tickets for a showing at a second.

body: The long-running art show will take place in the Los Angeles Convention Center’s West Hall downtown for its 32nd installment, Jan. 6-10. On view will be works from more than 90 exhibitors from across the United States and abroad.

articles.title: MNEK cancels tour over lack of ticket sales and high production costs
articles.summary: The Grammy-nominated artist was due to start a run of shows for his latest album Bulldozer!! next month.
body: MNEK has cancelled his upcoming tour due to a lack of ticket sales and the show not being "ready to the standard" he wanted.
In a statement shared on Instagram, the 31-year-old said he joins other artists who have cancelled shows recently as a result of "high production costs" and "over-ambitious planning".
Earlier this year, The Pussycat Dolls called off almost the entire US leg of their reunion tour following poor ticket sales.
The singer, whose real name is Uzoechi Emenike, said he had been "really looking forward" to performing his new album but had "no interest in doing this tour if I can't do it right".
